<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bc496bf7d7c034690353352de308bed3c5a5c4c2` → `packageMentionDocs`.

This run read `content/docs` from `b0b9c1fe3a2002542d3742f7cb3cc4338698146b` — the merge of head `dc86f2a26809015e45c948c0c1086d6e2418feb3` into base `bc496bf7d7c034690353352de308bed3c5a5c4c2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

git fetch origin b0b9c1fe3a2002542d3742f7cb3cc4338698146b && git checkout b0b9c1fe3a2002542d3742f7cb3cc4338698146b

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `890ec13d9b798ed93baa9ba4d642f44f572fdb7f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/services/service-analytics/src/measure-currency-coherence.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/__tests__/record-currency-analytics.test.ts + packages/services/service-analytics/src/analytics-service.ts (`enrichResultColumns`, the currency chain the refusal text makes a claim about), packages/services/service-analytics/src/dataset-executor.ts (`computeDerived`, the derived `fields` entries), packages/services/service-analytics/src/dataset-compiler.ts (the one `compileDataset` call site), content/docs/data-modeling/currency.mdx (read for the claim it shares, not reviewed). The changeset is prose and is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

Inputs read: card #28019 (body, triage 6518908209, claim 6519052139 as amended, withdrawal 6519075426, os-dev-report 6520514172), PR #28043 body, file list and net diff against `main` `5aee206543c8`, the check-runs on the head at 2026-10-30T10:37Z. Ruling 6486427200 (ADR-0144 open item 12, letter A) and precedent #27991 / #28015 read as the cited code names them.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept set, narrowed — RIGHT. A derived `sum` / `difference` whose monetary operands all resolve to one `fixed` code (`resolvedOf`: every operand `kind: 'code'` with `fixed: true`, directly or through a derived sum built on them) and which declares another `currency` is now refused `DATASET_INVALID` / 400 (`measure-currency-coherence.ts:183-191`). Triage 6518908209 read ruling A's Shape 1 onto derived measures, in the same sentence; the branch implements that reading and nothing wider.
- Accept set, unchanged — RIGHT, each read in the code: a restated code (`resolved.code === m.currency`, control at test `:397-401`); operands resolving to no one `fixed` code (`fixed: false` once any operand is `tenant` or an explicit code over a `dynamic` field; a `ratio` / `product` resolves to `undefined`; control at `:403-413`); the record-mode arm at `:176-182` stands before the new branch; Guard 2 is untouched. A derived measure over two different `fixed` codes with its own `currency` resolves to `undefined`, skips the new branch and still falls to Guard 2 — right, since declaring a code does not make a mixed sum a number in any currency.
- Order of refusal — RIGHT. Guard 1 loops all measures before Guard 2, so a derived measure that is itself refused is named before a measure built on it; the message lists only monetary operands (`monetaryOperands` drops a `count`) and dedupes a repeated operand.
- Public surface — none moved. No export, no spec key, no new gate, no option on `compileDataset`; `skip-changeset` does not apply.
- Doors — RIGHT. The one `assertMeasureCurrenciesCoherent` call sits in `compileDataset` (`dataset-compiler.ts:860`), so registration, `queryDataset` and the draft preview refuse alike; the third `fixedShapes` row at test `:445` pins both request doors.

### ② Semver level

- `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` and `@objectstack/service-analytics` `minor` — RIGHT. AGENTS.md step 3: a value refused is `narrowed`; a kind takes at least `minor` on a package the diff moves. The claim's first `none` / `patch` was wrong on exactly that sentence, and the amendment before push corrected it; `check-changeset-no-major` reads `narrowed` beside a `(narrowing)` arm, and `Check Changeset` plus `Lint · CI, release & engine gates` are green on this head.
- The BREAKING banner and the ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` are present, and the category is the one ruling 6486427200 fixed for this refusal family (the prescription is the refusal message; nothing stored converts). RIGHT in form. ⛔ The prescription the marker leans on is the sentence ④ finds false, so the marker is honest only once that sentence is.
- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` — the arm is right, the value is not. `clause2-line.mjs:113-117`, the one reader: `yes (narrowing)` declares a diff that widens one surface AND narrows another; `no (narrowing)` declares "not a widening, but breaking". This diff widens nothing, so `no (narrowing)` is the truthful reading, and it is the spelling triage 6518908209 named. The dev followed ruling 6486427200's and #27991's `yes (narrowing)`; a precedent's spelling is not a reading. No gate distinguishes the two (`check-changeset-no-major` and `reviewFace` read the arm alone, so the tier and level stand either way) — should-fix, in the PR body and the changeset together.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none declared — none found.
- Claim amendment (declaration lines moved before push): judged in ② — level and kind right, value should-fix.
- `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` NOT-MEASURED locally: `Build Core` on the head is the gate; in progress at 2026-10-30T10:37Z.
- Out-of-scope finding "Skills-docs": the four texts from #28015 (`skills/objectstack-data/rules/field-types.md:185-187`, `skills/objectstack-ui/rules/dashboards.md:298-305`, `content/docs/data-modeling/currency.mdx:174-179`, `content/docs/api/data-api.mdx:505-510`) teach two `fixed` refusals and need the derived case — agreed. Triage asked for a `Skills-docs:` line on the PR; #27991 carried one (`Skills-docs: follow-up owed — paths`); this PR body carries none and the report names the carrier as "seat 4 or the skills lane". Should-fix: add the line and name the carrier. The follow-up must teach the corrected prescription from ④, and `currency.mdx:178` ("a derived `sum` or `difference` over one `fixed` code carries that code") needs qualifying — true of the compile-time resolution, false of the wire (④).
- Governed surfaces: none in the file list (`Governed Surface Queue Guard` green); the review is owed by the narrowing face alone. Docs Drift Check listed nothing (not a clean bill, by its own text).
- Check-runs on the head at 2026-10-30T10:37Z: success — Lint & Repo Gates and all seven `Lint ·` jobs, Type Check · source gates / consumer gates / debt ledger, Test Core (8/8), Test UI, Dogfood Regression Gate, Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Auto Label, Flag docs, Plan Test Core shards, filter; in progress — Build Core, Type Check · workspace, Test Core (1/8 to 7/8), Live E2E UI; the UI lint / typecheck / build jobs skipped (no `ui/` path). The gate verdict is not complete; nothing is red.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/services/service-analytics/src/measure-currency-coherence.ts`

- The condition holds against its cited code. `resolvedOf` (`:116-144`) is the compile-time half of the chain the header describes, `fixed` carried exactly as #27991 defined it; `computeDerived` (`dataset-executor.ts:277-296`) adds and subtracts bare operand numbers, so a `sum` of EUR amounts is EUR amounts and a declared `USD` would label them wrongly — the refusal is right, and its scenario (card #28019's `eur_a + eur_b` as `USD`) is pinned at test `:373-388`.
- Tried to break it: a derived measure over a `fixed` operand and an explicit same code over a `dynamic` field resolves `fixed: false` and is not judged (consistent with the ruling's not-judged list); a self-referencing derived measure is cut by `resolving`; a repeated operand prints once; a derived measure declaring a currency over a derived measure that itself declares a contradicting one is refused at the inner measure first. All hold.
- **MUST-FIX — the prescription is false against the cited chain.** The message ends "delete the measure's `currency` (the column takes the operands' EUR)", and the changeset repeats "the column takes the operands' code". Read `enrichResultColumns`, `analytics-service.ts:3194-3209`: `meta` is read through `m.field`, a derived measure has no `field`, so `meta` is `undefined` and `monetary = !!mc.currency || meta?.type === 'currency'` is false the moment the author deletes `currency`. The derived column (`dataset-executor.ts:1335` mints it as a bare `type: 'number'` field) then carries NO currency code on the wire: the author who follows the prescription turns a wrongly labelled money column into an unlabelled one, and the only spelling that yields a labelled EUR column today is to RESTATE `currency: 'EUR'` — the control at `:397-401` accepts it and the chain labels it (`mc.currency`). That is the opposite of what the text says. The same sentence is true for the aggregated arm (`:170-172`: the field's `defaultCurrency` labels the column) and was copied across without reading the derived case of the chain. A refusal prescription is a runtime string shown to authors and ships in `CHANGELOG.md` (AGENTS.md: the lesson goes into the text; Prime Directive 10: declared ≠ delivered), so this is must-fix, not wording. Fix: say what the runtime does — "restate the operands' EUR, or delete the measure's `currency` (the column then carries no currency code)" — in the message and the changeset, and move the pinned sentence at test `:385-386` with it. Not to fold in: the gap itself (a derived sum over one `fixed` code labelled by nothing on the wire, while `currency.mdx:178` says it carries that code) is a runtime finding for its own card (Prime Directive 10), and the `Skills-docs:` follow-up should teach the corrected prescription.
- Should-fix: none further in this file; the header (`:19-23`) and the Guard 1 comment (`:152-154`) describe the arm correctly.

`packages/services/service-analytics/src/__tests__/record-currency-analytics.test.ts`

- The pins hold the scenario: both ops, the message head and the prescription tail (`:373-388`), the next-level derived operand (`:390-395`), the two controls (`:397-413`) and the two request doors (`:445`). The red-first count in the report (5) matches the pins the diff adds whose assertions the old tree fails (two ops, one next-level, two doors); the controls are green on both trees, as a control should be.
- Must-fix (same finding): `:385-386` asserts the false prescription verbatim and must follow the message.
- Should-fix (nit): the file header `:22-27` still says the guard refuses a measure `currency` "contradicting a `fixed` field's code"; add the derived operands' code, as the module header now does.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-kwainq`
Reviewed-by: `session_016WV4d1Np3hU7RQnA13YZcL`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

One must-fix: the derived-arm prescription ("the column takes the operands' EUR") is false against `enrichResultColumns`; correct it in the message, the changeset and the pinned test sentence. Should-fix: `Clause-②` value `no (narrowing)` on both carriers; a `Skills-docs:` line naming the four texts and the carrier; the test-file header. A head carrying those re-owes a record; the arm's logic itself holds and needs no change.
